entity_title: EU/EFTA registration with the commune within 14 days
fact_text: As an EU/EFTA national you must register with the local authorities of the commune where you live within 14 days of arrival and before you take up work, and apply for a residence permit.
evidence_quote: Within 14 days of their arrival and before actually taking up work, nationals of EU/EFTA states have to register with the local authorities of the commune in which they are residing and apply for a residence permit.

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed: free movement means an EU/EFTA citizen just arrives and starts work. Actually: you must register with your commune within 14 days and before starting work, and apply for a residence permit. Action required: book the commune registration (Anmeldung) immediately on arrival in Zurich.

entity_title: EU/EFTA residence permit type (L / B) by employment length
fact_text: As an EU/EFTA national your residence permit type depends on the length of employment: a short-term L permit for employment up to 364 days, or a B permit for employment of at least one year or of unlimited duration.
evidence_quote: A residence permit will be issued depending on the duration of employment: a short-term residence permit (type L permit) for employment of up to 364 days or a residence permit (type B permit) for employment of at least one year or for an unlimited period.

entity_title: Working up to 3 months without a permit (notification)
fact_text: As an EU/EFTA national you may work in Switzerland for up to three months in a calendar year without a residence permit, but the employment is subject to the notification (online registration) procedure with the authorities.
evidence_quote: EU/EFTA nationals taking up a job in Switzerland may stay in Switzerland without a residence permit for three months in a calendar year. However, they are subject to notification with the appropriate authorities.

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed: any work in Switzerland needs a permit first. Actually: EU/EFTA nationals can work up to three months per calendar year without a residence permit, but the employer must file an online notification. Action required: ensure the employer completes the notification before work starts.

entity_title: Work permit required for any gainful activity (third-country)
fact_text: As a non-EU/EFTA (third-country) national you need a permit to carry out any gainful activity in Switzerland, irrespective of the length of your stay.
evidence_quote: Ausländerinnen und Ausländer, die in der Schweiz eine Erwerbstätigkeit ausüben wollen, benötigen unabhängig von der Aufenthaltsdauer eine Bewilligung.

entity_title: Permits only for managers, specialists, qualified workers (third-country)
fact_text: As a non-EU/EFTA national, Swiss short-stay and residence permits for gainful employment may only be granted to managers, specialists and other qualified workers.
evidence_quote: Kurzaufenthalts- und Aufenthaltsbewilligungen zur Ausübung einer Erwerbstätigkeit können nur Führungskräften, Spezialistinnen und Spezialisten und anderen qualifizierten Arbeitskräften erteilt werden.

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed: any job offer lets a non-EU worker move to Switzerland. Actually: third-country permits are restricted to managers, specialists and other qualified workers. Action required: confirm the role qualifies as highly skilled before planning the move.

entity_title: Labour-market priority for third-country hires
fact_text: As a non-EU/EFTA national you can only be admitted for employment if the employer shows that no suitable worker from Switzerland or from a state with a free-movement agreement could be found for the post.
evidence_quote: Ausländerinnen und Ausländer können zur Ausübung einer Erwerbstätigkeit nur zugelassen werden, wenn nachgewiesen wird, dass keine dafür geeigneten inländischen Arbeitnehmerinnen und Arbeitnehmer oder Angehörige von Staaten, mit denen ein Freizügigkeitsabkommen abgeschlossen wurde, gefunden werden können.

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed: if a company wants to hire you, that is enough. Actually: the employer must first prove no suitable Swiss/EU-EFTA candidate was available (labour-market priority). Action required: expect the employer to document its recruitment search as part of the permit file.

entity_title: Federal quotas on third-country work permits
fact_text: As a non-EU/EFTA national your first Swiss short-stay/residence permit for gainful employment is subject to federal quotas: the Federal Council may cap the number of first-time work permits.
evidence_quote: Der Bundesrat kann die Zahl der erstmaligen Kurzaufenthalts- und Aufenthaltsbewilligungen (Art. 32 und 33) zur Ausübung einer Erwerbstätigkeit begrenzen.

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed: a qualifying job guarantees a permit. Actually: third-country work permits are rationed by annual federal quotas that can run out. Action required: plan timing with the employer, as start dates can depend on quota availability.

entity_title: Register with the authority before taking up work (third-country)
fact_text: As a non-EU/EFTA national who needs a permit you must register with the competent authority at your Swiss place of residence before the permit-free period ends or before you take up employment.
evidence_quote: Ausländerinnen und Ausländer, die eine Kurzaufenthalts-, Aufenthalts- oder Niederlassungsbewilligung benötigen, müssen sich vor Ablauf des bewilligungsfreien Aufenthalts oder vor der Aufnahme einer Erwerbstätigkeit bei der am Wohnort in der Schweiz zuständigen Behörde anmelden.

entity_title: Compulsory health insurance within 3 months (EU/EFTA)
fact_text: As an EU/EFTA national taking up residence in Switzerland you must take out basic health insurance (KVG/LAMal) within three months of arrival; cover then applies retroactively from your arrival date.
evidence_quote: Anyone settling in Switzerland must take out health insurance within three months after taking up residence.

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed: the employer or the state provides health cover automatically. Actually: everyone must buy individual basic insurance within three months of arriving; there is no automatic enrolment and each family member is insured separately. Action required: choose a KVG/LAMal insurer within three months.

entity_title: Compulsory health insurance within 3 months (third-country)

evidence_quote: Anyone settling in Switzerland must take out health insurance within three months after taking up residence.

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed: the employer or the state provides health cover automatically. entity_title: Compulsory AHV/AVS social security (EU/EFTA)
fact_text: As an EU/EFTA national gainfully employed in Switzerland you are compulsorily insured under the AHV/AVS (first-pillar old-age and survivors' insurance); you are given an AHV insurance number (756...) and your employer registers you and deducts contributions.
evidence_quote: die natürlichen Personen, die in der Schweiz eine Erwerbstätigkeit ausüben;

entity_title: Swiss tax residency and worldwide income (EU/EFTA)
fact_text: If you become tax-resident in Switzerland — by settling with intent to stay, or by staying at least 30 days while working (or 90 days without working) — you have unlimited Swiss tax liability on your worldwide income, except for foreign businesses, permanent establishments and real estate.
evidence_quote: Bei persönlicher Zugehörigkeit ist die Steuerpflicht unbeschränkt; sie erstreckt sich aber nicht auf Geschäftsbetriebe, Betriebsstätten und Grundstücke im Ausland.

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed: Switzerland uses a 183-day rule and only taxes your Swiss salary. Actually: Swiss domestic law triggers tax residence after a 30-day stay with gainful activity (or 90 days without), and residents are taxed on worldwide income. Action required: check the applicable double-taxation treaty and your move date.

entity_title: EU right to reside over 3 months as a worker
fact_text: As an EU citizen you have the right to reside in Italy for more than three months when you are an employed or self-employed worker in the country (D.Lgs 30/2007, art. 7, lett. a).
evidence_quote: Il cittadino dell'Unione ha diritto di soggiornare nel territorio nazionale per un periodo superiore a tre mesi quando:

entity_title: EU citizen municipal registration (iscrizione anagrafica) after 3 months
fact_text: As an EU citizen staying in Italy for more than three months you must obtain iscrizione anagrafica (registration in the resident-population registry) at your comune; registration is required once three months from entry have passed, and an attestation is issued immediately.
evidence_quote: Fermo quanto previsto dal comma 1, l'iscrizione è comunque richiesta trascorsi tre mesi dall'ingresso ed è rilasciata immediatamente una attestazione contenente l'indicazione del nome e della dimora del richiedente, nonché la data della richiesta.

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed: an EU citizen has nothing to file in Italy. Actually: staying beyond three months creates a duty to obtain iscrizione anagrafica at your comune, and the attestation is needed for many later procedures. Action required: register at the Milan comune once you have an address.

entity_title: Work authorization (nulla osta al lavoro) for non-EU hires
fact_text: To hire a non-EU national resident abroad for subordinate employment, the employer must file a specific (nominativa) application for a nulla osta al lavoro (work authorization) at the Sportello Unico per l'Immigrazione (SUI) competent for the province where the work will be performed.
evidence_quote: Per instaurare un rapporto di lavoro subordinato con un cittadino extracomunitario residente all'estero, infatti, il datore di lavoro - italiano o straniero legalmente soggiornante in Italia - deve presentare richiesta nominativa di nulla osta al lavoro al Sui competente per la provincia nella quale si svolgerà l'attività lavorativa.

entity_title: Permesso di soggiorno within 8 working days of entry
fact_text: As a non-EU national you must apply for your permesso di soggiorno within 8 working days (excluding Sundays and public holidays) of entering Italy.
evidence_quote: Il permesso di soggiorno va richiesto entro 8 giorni lavorativi (esclusi quindi la domenica e i festivi).

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed: the entry visa is enough to settle in Italy. Actually: you must apply for the permesso di soggiorno within 8 working days of arrival, or your stay is at risk. Action required: file the permesso kit at a Poste Italiane Sportello Amico immediately after arrival.

entity_title: Mandatory SSN registration for non-EU workers
fact_text: As a non-EU national regularly staying in Italy with an employment relationship you have the obligation to register with the Servizio Sanitario Nazionale (SSN), with equal treatment and full equality of rights and duties compared with Italian citizens.
evidence_quote: Hanno l'obbligo di iscrizione al Servizio sanitario nazionale e hanno parità di trattamento e piena uguaglianza di diritti e doveri rispetto ai cittadini italiani

entity_title: Codice fiscale (tax/identity code) — EU
fact_text: The codice fiscale is the tool that identifies natural persons in all dealings with Italian public bodies and administrations; you need one to work, sign a lease, open a bank account and access the health service.
evidence_quote: Il codice fiscale è lo strumento di identificazione delle persone fisiche e dei soggetti diversi dalle persone fisiche in tutti i rapporti con gli enti e le amministrazioni pubbliche.

entity_title: Codice fiscale (tax/identity code) — third-country

entity_title: Italian tax residency — 183 days (EU)
fact_text: You are considered resident in Italy for income-tax purposes if, for the greater part of the year (at least 183 days, 184 in leap years), you meet at least one condition: habitual abode, domicile, physical presence, or registration in the resident-population registry in Italy.
evidence_quote: È residente in Italia ai fini delle imposte sui redditi chi, per la maggior parte dell'anno (almeno 183 giorni l'anno, 184 in quelli bisestili), soddisfa almeno una delle seguenti condizioni

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed: you only become an Italian taxpayer if you register there. Actually: tax residency is triggered by any one of several tests met for most of the year (183 days) — including mere physical presence or having your domicile/centre of personal ties in Italy. Action required: track your days and check the double-taxation treaty.

entity_title: Residents taxed on worldwide income (EU)
fact_text: Once resident in Italy for tax purposes you are taxed on your worldwide income: the tax applies to the taxpayer's total income, made up — for residents — of all income possessed, and — for non-residents — only of income produced in Italy.
evidence_quote: L'imposta si applica sul reddito complessivo del soggetto, formato per i residenti da tutti i redditi posseduti al netto degli oneri deducibili indicati nell'articolo 10 e per i non residenti soltanto da quelli prodotti nel territorio dello Stato.

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed: Italy only taxes your Italian salary. Actually: an Italian tax resident is taxed on worldwide income (all income possessed), while non-residents are taxed only on Italian-source income. Action required: plan your residency start and check the applicable treaty.

entity_title: EU/EEA right of residence — no residence permit
fact_text: As an EU/EEA citizen you have the right of residence — the right to work, run your own business, study or live in Sweden without a residence permit — provided you can support yourself; you do not need to contact the Swedish Migration Agency.
evidence_quote: If you are an EU/EEA citizen, you have the right to work, run your own business, study or live in Sweden without a residence permit.

entity_title: EU/EEA citizens may start working on arrival
fact_text: As an EU/EEA citizen you may start working (or running a business or studying) in Sweden directly, as soon as you arrive — no work permit and no waiting period.
evidence_quote: As an EU/EEA citizen, you have the right to start working, running your own business or studying directly as soon as you arrive in Sweden.

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed: you must wait for paperwork before starting a job abroad. Actually: an EU/EEA citizen can start working in Sweden immediately on arrival; the key first step is registering with the Tax Agency for a personnummer, not the Migration Agency. Action required: line up the Skatteverket registration early.

entity_title: Work permit required (non-EU/EEA)
fact_text: As a citizen of a country outside the EU/EEA you will in most cases need a work permit to work in Sweden.
evidence_quote: If you are a citizen of a country outside the EU/EEA, you will in most cases need a permit to work in Sweden.

entity_title: Work permit needed even for intra-group transfers
fact_text: As a non-EU/EEA national you need a work permit to work in Sweden regardless of whether you are employed in Sweden or abroad, hired out by a temporary employment agency, or transferred within a group (intra-corporate transfer).
evidence_quote: If you are going to work in Sweden, you need a work permit regardless of whether you are employed in Sweden or abroad, if you are employed by a temporary employment agency that hires out labour to a business in Sweden, or if you have been transferred within a group.

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed: an intra-company transfer or a foreign contract avoids the Swedish work permit. Actually: a permit is required even when you stay on a foreign payroll, are hired out by an agency, or are transferred within your own group. Action required: secure the permit before relocating, whatever the contract structure.

entity_title: EU Blue Card for highly qualified employment
fact_text: As a highly qualified non-EU/EEA professional you may apply for an EU Blue Card, which gives the right to live and work in Sweden; it requires higher education corresponding to at least 180 higher-education credits (or at least five years of relevant professional experience) and a salary at or above the threshold Migrationsverket sets.
evidence_quote: Your higher education must correspond to at least 180 higher education credits. Alternatively, you can have at least five years of relevant professional experience.

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed: the ordinary work permit is the only route. Actually: highly qualified hires can use the EU Blue Card (needs a degree or 5 years' experience plus a salary above the annually-set threshold), which carries stronger mobility and family rights. Action required: check whether the Blue Card is a better fit than the standard work permit.

entity_title: Population register (folkbokföring) and personnummer (EU/EEA)
fact_text: If you move to Sweden and plan to live here for one year or more you should be listed in the Swedish Population Register (folkbokföring) at Skatteverket; when first listed you are assigned a Swedish personal identity number (personnummer), needed for almost everything in daily life.
evidence_quote: you should be listed in the Swedish Population Register if you have moved to Sweden and plan to live here for one year or more.

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed: EU free movement means no registration in Sweden. Actually: if you will live in Sweden for a year or more you should register in the population register at Skatteverket, and that is how you get your personnummer. Action required: book the in-person 'Moving to Sweden' registration at a service centre.

entity_title: Population register (folkbokföring) and personnummer (third-country)
fact_text: If you move to Sweden and plan to live here for one year or more you should be listed in the Swedish Population Register (folkbokföring) at Skatteverket; when first listed you are assigned a Swedish personal identity number (personnummer), needed for almost everything in daily life.
evidence_quote: you should be listed in the Swedish Population Register if you have moved to Sweden and plan to live here for one year or more.

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed: the residence permit alone lets you function in Sweden. Actually: you also need to register in the population register at Skatteverket to get a personnummer, which is required for banking, healthcare and payroll. Action required: register at a Skatteverket service centre after arrival.

entity_title: Unlimited tax liability and worldwide income (EU/EEA)
fact_text: If you are domiciled in Sweden, stay here regularly (six consecutive months or more) or have significant connections to Sweden, you have unlimited tax liability — you are liable to Swedish tax on all your income, whether earned in Sweden or abroad.
evidence_quote: Persons who are domiciled in, stay regularly in or have significant connections to Sweden are subject to unlimited taxation in Sweden.

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed: Sweden only taxes your Swedish salary. Actually: being domiciled or staying six consecutive months makes you unlimitedly liable — taxed on all income wherever it originates. Action required: check the applicable double-taxation treaty and whether SINK/expert-tax relief applies.

entity_title: Swedish social insurance if you live or work here (EU/EEA)
fact_text: If you live or work in Sweden you are usually covered by Swedish social insurance and may be entitled to benefits from Försäkringskassan; what matters is where you live or work, not your citizenship. Residence-based benefits require being in the population register; work-based benefits require actually working here.
evidence_quote: If you live or work in Sweden, you are usually covered by Swedish social insurance and may be entitled to one or more benefits from Försäkringskassan.

entity_title: Swedish social insurance if you live or work here (third-country)
fact_text: If you live or work in Sweden you are usually covered by Swedish social insurance and may be entitled to benefits from Försäkringskassan; what matters is where you live or work, not your citizenship. Note that moving from outside the EU/EEA also requires a residence permit to be eligible for benefits.
evidence_quote: If you live or work in Sweden, you are usually covered by Swedish social insurance and may be entitled to one or more benefits from Försäkringskassan.
